title: A versioned open question, failed theorem, requirement record or promotion request
description: The four record types lean/registry/open-questions/ holds, as fixed by pipeline/leanbio/debate/CRITERIA.md 'Record types emitted (1.1.0)'. An open question is NEVER deleted: it is settled or abandoned, with the reason, and its file stays. Versioned exactly like a law (semver per record, content_hash over the hashed fields, history append-only).

evidence.description: One item of evidence for or against an arm. Every item cites a primary source and carries the sentence it rests on.

claim.description: what this item asserts, in plain English

source.description: authors, year, journal, and PMID/DOI where there is one

locator.description: where to find it: repo path with line or key, and the paper's figure/table/section

quote.description: VERBATIM. A record whose quote is a paraphrase misleads about what the source says.

kind.description: what sort of evidence: measurement, population regression, curated database mapping, computed metric, repo claim, Lean proof, ...

belief_class.description: the evidence class in pipeline/leanbio/belief-params.json; fixes this item's rand/syst in the belief formula

belief_key.description: the independence key (a DOI, PMID, claim id, draft path or law id). Items sharing a key count ONCE. Defaults to `source` when absent.

side.description: whether this item supports or contradicts THE ARM IT IS LISTED UNDER

quote_kind.description: e.g. 'full text', 'abstract only', 'secondhand (the later paper restates the earlier record)'

position.description: 'for', 'against', or a named alternative (e.g. 'biphasic'). A question with a genuine third position names it rather than forcing two sides.

lean_ref.description: the Lean declaration that states this arm, when it has been formalised. null when it has not, and `formalisable` then says whether it could be.

built.description: how and when it was compiled, and the axioms printed

formalisable.description: can this arm be stated as a named hypothesis over quantities a design or an observation could carry? false needs a reason in `not_formalisable_because`.

belief.description: COMPUTED by openq-lib.mjs from `evidence` via pipeline/leanbio/belief.mjs. Never hand-written; recompute() overwrites it.

belief_basis.description: the breakdown the belief formula returned: E, R, per-class counts, and the params version. Reproducible, not asserted.

arms.description: At least TWO arms. A one-armed open question is not a question, it is an unsupported claim, and openq-lib.mjs rejects it.

proportion.description: the belief split across arms, COMPUTED from the arms' evidence by pipeline/leanbio/belief.mjs so it is reproducible rather than asserted.

shares.description: arm_id -> share of total belief, 3 decimals, summing to 1

settles_in_favour_of.description: the arm_id this observation would select, or 'either' when the observation's VALUE decides

touches.description: what in this project rests on the answer. The Studio uses it to flag a verdict as resting on an unsettled question.

guard.description: how the guard recognises a law that asserts an arm. Signatures are conservative token sets, not NLP.

dispute_id.description: the matching id in open-disputes.json, so the two lists cannot drift apart silently

arm_signatures.description: arm_id -> {all_of:[tokens], none_of?:[tokens]}. A law whose statement contains EVERY all_of token (and no none_of token) is treated as asserting that arm.

scoped_exemptions.description: law_ids allowed to state ONE arm because they are narrowed to the preparation that arm was measured in, so they do not assert the disputed general claim. A two-sided handshake: the law file must ALSO carry open_question_scoped naming this question, or the exemption does not apply. This is the only way past the guard short of settling the question.

how.description: the narrowing that makes the law not an assertion of the arm

approved_by_role.description: a role, never a personal identifier

exclusivity.description: whether the arms actually contradict. Forcing a contradiction where there is none misrepresents the sources.

premise.description: for 'proved-under-premise': the added empirical premise the contradiction needs, which is itself unestablished

settled.description: REQUIRED when status is 'settled': which arm survived and WHICH EVIDENCE settled it.

retired_arms.description: the arm_ids the settling evidence eliminated. Kept, never deleted.

abandoned.description: REQUIRED when status is 'abandoned': why the question was given up rather than answered.

found_by.description: how this question came to be recorded. Worth keeping: several were found by trying to FORMALISE a dispute, which is an argument for formalisation as a method.

failedTheorem.description: A statement we tried to establish and could not. Kept so nobody reproposes it, and so the failure is a result rather than a gap.

statement_en.description: the statement that was attempted, as attempted

reason.description: the category of failure. 'provable-but-not-checkable' is NOT a rejection: CRITERIA.md routes it to a requirements record, and it appears here only when the missing inputs are known to be unobtainable.

what_survives.description: what is still true after the failure. A failure record that says only 'it failed' throws away the result.

lean_ref.description: the attempted declaration, if one was written

became_open_question.description: question_id, when the failure turned out to be a live two-sided question rather than a settled negative

requirements.description: CRITERIA.md 'candidate-with-requirements': a NEEDS-WORK ruling, including the 'provable but not checkable' case (a sound statement with no shared scope, so the Studio has nothing to evaluate). NOT a failure: the referee's list of what would make it promotable travels with the law.

missing_inputs.description: the quantities a design would have to carry for this to bind

promotionRequest.description: CRITERIA.md 'promotion-request': queued for a human. The law itself is already in the registry as `candidate`; promotion to `accepted` is never automated.

blocked_by_open_questions.description: question_ids the guard found this law asserting an arm of. Non-empty means it is NOT promotable.
